en: My ancestors, the old men and women folk, were of the Mexican People Clan. With great hardship they came back from the place called Fort Sumner, packing their goods on their backs, and afterward lived here at Lukachukai.
nv: shadahastóí ńtʼééʼ, índa dashimá sání ńtʼééʼ, naakaii dineʼé danilį́įgo, hojoobáʼígo hwééldi hoolyéédę́ę́ʼ ninádaʼiishjidgo kwii lókʼaʼjígai hoolyéegi kéédahatʼį́į́ ńtʼééʼ.

en: Here they began life anew.
nv: kodóó shį́į́ haakai nahalin silį́į́ʼ.

en: Then from their home at a place called Spring in the Clay they started moving over and across yonder mountain.
nv: dleesh biiʼ tó hoolyéegi dahooghan ńtʼéeʼgo dah adiiná jiní nagháí dził báátis góʼąą.

en: While they were making this move they stopped for the night, and it is said that I was born where they halted.
nv: ákǫ́ǫ́ oonéełgo dahwiiłkaahgo ákwii shiʼdizhchį́ jiní.

en: Let’s see, I believe it was in the month of October.
nv: ghąąjįʼ wolyéego ńdízídígíí daashin tʼáá éí biyiʼ jiní.

en: I was born on a night when a heavy snow had begun to fall.
nv: tłʼéeʼgo hááhgóóshį́į́ deezhchxíilgo tsʼídá ákóneʼ shiʼdizhchį́ jiní.

en: My grandfather, a man by the name of White Mexican Clansman, and another man called The Son of Former
nv: shicheii ńtʼééʼ naakai dineʼé łigaii wolyéé ńtʼééʼ dóó łaʼ dóʼ diné táchéhéniʼ biyeʼ wolyéé ńtʼééʼ éí shį́į́ tʼéiyá diné nilį́įgo dóó sáanii dóʼ díkwíí shį́į́ kwii shaa naanish bííghą́ą́ʼ.
sweathouse, were the only men. they and several womenfolk worked hard on me.	from a navajo corpus of historical narratives 2.3

en: My grandfather had a fine wether goat that he was quite proud of. He killed it there, and the people feasted with
nv: shicheii tłʼízí choʼádinii ayói da átʼé halį́į́ʼ ńtʼéeʼgo éí ákwii jiisxį́įgo hááhgóóshį́į́ diné bił dahózhǫ́ǫgo daʼoolghal jiní.
great joy.	from a navajo corpus of historical narratives 3.1

en: Then on the day following the night of my birth we again started to move.
nv: tłʼéédą́ą́ʼ shiʼdizhchį́įgo tʼáá áko dah nááʼdiiʼná jiní.

en: In those days people went about only on horseback or on foot.
nv: íídą́ą́ʼ łį́į́ʼ tʼéiyá bee ndaʼaldeehgo tʼáá niʼ dóʼ.

en: On the day following the night on which she gave birth to me, my mother went on foot as far as the people moved that day.
nv: shimá tłʼéédą́ą́ʼ shijishchį́įgo tʼáá niʼ jiníyá jiní níwohjįʼ haa shį́į́ nízahgi niʼínéehgo áajįʼ.

en: And since it had snowed the night before they had to go through the snow.
nv: tłʼéédą́ą́ʼ yidzaazgo yas biyiʼ íldeé jiní.

en: It is remarkable how risky life was in those days.
nv: haʼátʼíí shį́į́ yówéé átʼéego diné tʼáá bizááká kéédahatʼį́į́ ńtʼééʼ lá íídą́ą́ʼ.

en: Nowadays when a woman gives birth they take special care of her, telling her not to catch cold.
nv: kʼadgo éiyá ajiłchíihgo hakʼaz biih wolyeed lágo haʼníigo hońdahodéeníih.

en: Back at that time it was different.
nv: íídą́ą́ʼ éí doo ákótʼée da ńtʼééʼ lá.

en: As time went on I somehow grew up. I do not remember much about it.
nv: áádóó wóshdeę́ę́ʼ haa shį́į́ yitʼéego shiyaa hazlį́į́ʼ, éí doo tsʼídá hazhóʼó bénáshniih da.

en: I do not remember in detail much of what happened before I was about ten years old.
nv: neeznáá daatsʼí shinááhai dóó índa tʼáá kóníghání nahalingo énáshniihgo hodideeshzhiizh.

en: When morning would come and I would be sleeping nicely, my grandfather would throw me out of bed.
nv: áyąą ahbínígo nizhónígo ashhoshę́ę shicheii náshidiyiiłhą́ą́h.

en: “Come on! Come on!
nv: “nahgóó, nahgóó.

en: Why are you lying down?
nv: haʼátʼíí biniiyé sínítį́?

en: Go run a race.
nv: nahgóó dághádílyeed.

en: If you're weak the first harmful thing that comes along will run over you.
nv: dinigisgo háadi shį́į́ deeteel tʼáá áłtsé silį́ʼígíí nikʼi chʼídoolwoł.

en: If you are strong you will lie hudled in death only after the dirt is torn and furrowed around you,” my grandfather used to tell me.
nv: honíyóigo éí łeezh naańdaasdláadgo áadi índa shíníljool dooleeł,” jiníi łeh ńtʼééʼ shicheii yę́ę.

en: The old folks all used to say that.
nv: índa hastóí tʼáá ałtso ákódajiníi łeh ńtʼééʼ.

en: They probably said this because they knew of the wars that were going on.
nv: eíshąʼ ana dahólóonii hoł béédahózingo ádajiníí ńtʼééʼ.

en: That is the way my grandfather drove me about and spoke to me.
nv: shicheii yę́ę ákótʼéego tʼáá nashineeyood dóó tʼáá shichʼįʼ yááłtiʼ.

en: He did not speak in anger.
nv: doo hashkéego áníi da.

en: He did not speak harshly.
nv: doo tʼáá naʼníleʼee áníi da.

en: He told it to me in a nice way.
nv: hazhóóʼógo áshiłníí ńtʼééʼ.

en: So that is the way I spent my days from that time on.
nv: jó éí áádę́ę́ʼ ákótʼéego shíiníłką́.

en: After I had reached the age of eighteen I did various kinds of odd jobs.
nv: tseebíítsʼáadah shinááhai sélį́įʼgo, áajįʼ aníísą́ągo, jó kodóó shinaanish naatʼiʼ tʼáá bihoniyázhígi.

en: I had an uncle by the name of Forked House. He was a young man, and he adopted me.
nv: shidáʼí ńtʼééʼ tʼiisyaa bikiní wolyéé ńtʼééʼ, tsíłkę́ę́h nilį́įgo, éí áyaa nikishidiiltʼeʼ.

en: He started sending me on chores.
nv: nikishidiiłʼaʼ.

en: I would take care of his horses for him.
nv: łį́į́ʼ bá naasłóozgo.

en: He had a wagon and a team.
nv: bitsinaabąąs hólǫ́ǫgo, bilį́į́ʼ naʼałbąąsii hólǫ́ǫgo.

en: He would tell me to haul wood with it, or to work with it.
nv: díí bee chizh nihíyeeh, díí bee nanilnish shiłníigo.

en: At the time I was about eighteen years old the person who started the present trading post at Blue Clay Point moved there - I used to know just when it was.
nv: tsʼídá tseebíítsʼáadah shinááhaigo bis dootłʼizh deezʼáhí hoolyéegi, kʼad naalyéhé bá hooghan, ninínáanii tʼáá shił bééhózin ńtʼééʼ.

en: They used to call the Former Old Interpreter Chee when I first heard of him.
nv: hastiin adiitsʼaʼí yę́ęniʼ chííʼ dabijiníí lágo baa ákoniizį́į́ʼ.

en: Chee was a good friend of a white man from Ugly House known as Big Lump Setting Up.
nv: kin hóchxǫ́ʼí hoolyéédę́ę́ʼ bilagáana dah shizhóód wolyéé ńtʼééʼ éí shį́į́ chííʼ ayóigo bichʼooní ńtʼééʼ lá.

en: Well, finally.
nv: jó éí abáágago.

en: The two of them built the trading post at the place called Blue Clay Point.
nv: áko éí yaa ndiltʼéego bis dootłʼizh deezʼáhí hoolyéegi naalyéhé bá hooghan áhoolaa.

en: It was in the Spring when they moved there.
nv: dąągo ákwii niʼníná.

en: There was an epidemic in progress, and we now refer to it as "the time when the throat killed many."
nv: naałniih, dinékʼehjígo “hayaayááh dahóóghánę́ędą́ą́ʼ” dabidiiʼní kʼad.

en: It was at that time, in the spring, that they moved to Blue Clay Point, it was said.
nv: íídą́ą́ʼ dąągo tʼah ńtʼééʼ bis dootłʼizh deezʼáhí hoolyéegi niʼníná hodooʼniid.

en: That is how it came about that the one who would be called The Interpreter and the one who would be named Big Lump Setting Up came to move there.
nv: kʼadshąʼ hastiin adiitsʼaʼii yidoolyeeł léiʼ, dah shizhóód yidoolyeeł léiʼ, kótʼéego ákǫ́ǫ́ ninínáá lá.

en: They built the trading post and four years later perhaps, I do not recall exactly when, the one I called my uncle
nv: naalyéhé bá hooghan áhoolyaa dóó dį́į́ʼ daatsʼí éí nááhaigo ákwii doo hazhóʼó bénáshniih da, tʼah ńtʼééʼ naalyéhé bá hooghandi chizh nihoheeh nihizhdííniid shidáʼí ńtʼééʼ dishnínígíí.
told us to haul wood there.	from a navajo corpus of historical narratives 10.1

en: They probably called for the wood.
nv: áádę́ę́’ shį́į́ chizh ho’doo’niidgo.

en: There was a boy of the Big Water Clan with whom I always chummed around.
nv: ashkii łaʼ tótsohnii nilį́įgo tʼáá áłahjįʼ bił tádíshʼaash, éí hoł.

en: We started doing that kind of work.
nv: aadóó aají nihinaanish deeztʼiʼ.

en: We went about calling each other “my younger brother,” and we hauled wood to the trading post.
nv: sitsilí ahidiiʼníigo tádiitʼaash. naalyéhé bá hooghangi chizh nihiigeeh.

en: We heard reports that there were people going about to get children put into school.
nv: áłchíní óltaʼjįʼ ndahaʼníiłgo baa naʼaldeeh jiní haʼníigo yiiʼniiʼ.

en: It was said that they were then over at Chinle, and we heard that they were coming here sometime soon.
nv: chʼínílį́į́jí baa naʼaldeeh jiní. hahgo shį́į́ kwii bił ínééh jiní haʼníigo yiiʼniiʼ.

en: We would discuss it when we took the wagon after wood.
nv: áádóó baa yiníitʼį́įgo chizh haʼiilbąąs.

en: “Say, let's go to school,” I said to my companion.
nv: “ashkihéi íídíiltah,” hodííniid hoł naashʼaash yę́ę.

en: “All right,” he said.
nv: “hágoshį́į́,” jidííniid.

en: And we went about, talking enthusiastically about it.
nv: aadóó baa yiníitʼį́įgo baa nihił hózhǫ́ǫgo tádiitʼaash.

en: In the evening after we had unloaded another load of wood we started back home in the wagon.
nv: iʼííʼą́ągo chizh bida nááheeʼnilgo hooghangóó dah ńʼdiilbą́ą́z.

en: When we got back to home we found that my uncle was there.
nv: hooghandi nániitʼáázh ńtʼééʼ shidáʼí yę́ę sidáá lá.

en: And it turned out that my grandfather, who was called Big Mexican Clansman, was there too.
nv: shicheii naakaii dineʼétsoh wolyéé ńtʼééʼ éí dóʼ sidáá lá.

en: So we told them of our plan.
nv: áko ákweʼé bee bił hwiilneʼ.

en: “They are putting children in school,” it is said.
nv: “áłchíní óltaʼjįʼ ndahaʼnííł,” jiní.

en: We told them how we had both said, “Let's go to school.”
nv: “tʼáá áníidlah íídíiltah diiʼniid,” diiʼníigo bee hoł hwiilneʼ.

en: “It's probably all right. It's fine indeed, my children. A party is in its way coming to us. You cannot escape them anyway,” my uncle and my grandfather said to us.
nv: “tʼáá shį́į́ áko. háadish dóʼ baa dáádidoohʼash,” nihizhdííniid shidáʼí yę́ę dóó shicheiiaa dáádidoohʼash,” nihizhdííniid shidáʼí yę́ę dóó shicheii yę́ę.

en: On the next day we went to the trading post, and my grandfather put his thumbprint on a paper for us.
nv: biiskání naalyéhé bá hooghangóó niikai dóó shicheii yę́ę naaltsoos nihá bizhdeelchid.

en: It was reported that the children from Chinle who were being taken to school would get there in two days, and
nv: naaki yiską́ągo chʼínílį́į́dę́ę́ʼ áłchíní óltaʼgóó dadeeshtʼeezhígíí kwii bił íbąąs haʼníigo hastóí nihinááł yee ałchʼįʼ hadaasdzííʼ.
we heard the grownups talking to one another about it.	from a navajo corpus of historical narratives 16.2

en: Of those men who were talking to one another about it, one was called Weela. He lived over behind Round Rock and was one of the leaders at that time.
nv: yee ałchʼįʼ hadaasdzíiʼii hastóí łaʼ wéela wolyéé ńtʼééʼ tsénikání yineʼjí kéédahatʼį́į́ ńtʼééʼ. íídąąʼ éí naatʼáanii danilį́įgo.

en: One was called Bead Clan Gambler, and he was a member of the police force.
nv: yoo’ó ’adika’í wolyéé ńt’éé’, éí dó’ siláago ’atah nilį́įgo.

en: He was a very strong man.
nv: ayóo baa dzólníigo óolyéé ńtʼééʼ.

en: He was from Chinle, but he was a member of the police force at Fort Defiance.
nv: chʼínílį́į́dóó naagháa ndi tséhootsooídi siláago atah nilį́į́ ńtʼééʼ.

en: He had come on ahead with the white man from Fort Defiance called Little Chief.
nv: éí tséhootsooídóó bilagáana naatʼáanii yázhí wolyéé ńtʼééʼ alą́ąjįʼ yił yíkai lá.

en: It was there that my grandfather promised us.
nv: akwii shicheii ńtʼééʼ nihee hajoodzííʼ.

en: “I am putting these two boys in school,”  he said by way of promise.
nv: “shí díí ashiiké naakigo óltaʼjįʼ ninishnííł,” jiníigo bee hajoodzííʼ.

en: Since it was reported that it would be another day before the wagon load of children would arrive, we went back
nv: yiską́ągo índa áłchíní bił íbąąs haʼníigo tʼóó hooghangóó nániikai.
home.	from a navajo corpus of historical narratives 19.1

en: We spent the night there and then returned on foot.
nv: áadi danihiiską́ągo áádę́ę́ʼ tʼáá niʼ náániikai.

en: And we found that the children had arrived.
nv: ńtʼééʼ áłchíní bił aníbą́ą́z lá.

en: There was some man of the Bitter Water Clan whom people called Pug Nose. He was going around with the
nv: hastiin léiʼ tó díchʼíiʼnii nilį́į́ ńtʼééʼ chį́shchʼį́į́d dabijiníí ńtʼééʼ éí áłchíní yaa áhályą́ągo bił naʼaldeeh lá.
party, taking care of the children.	from a navajo corpus of historical narratives 20.2

en: He knew a little English, and that was probably why he was told to take care of the children.
nv: tʼáá áłchʼį́į́dígo bilagáana bizaad bił bééhózin ńtʼééʼ. éí shį́į́ bąą áłchíní baa áhólyą́ą dooleeł biʼdooʼniid.

en: Chattering in English, he was busily running around the children who had been hauled in,
nv: bilagáanakʼeh yádíłtihgo áłchíní yígínę́ę hááhgóóshį́į́ yináálwoł.

en: He was keeping them together.
nv: ahaninéíʼniłgo yaa naaghá.

en: The children from Blue Clay Point who were to be put in school had not all been brought in as yet.
nv: bis dootłʼizh deezʼáhí binaagi áłchíní ndayiiznilii tʼah doo ałtso ndayiiʼéesh da.

en: In two days, it was said that the wagon with the children would start off.
nv: áko naaki yiską́ągo índa bił dah adidoobąs hodooʼniid.

en: They were to go by way of Lukachukai, Tsaile, and Crystal, and on over to Fort Defiance.
nv: nagháí lókʼaʼjíkai góneʼ dóó tsééhílį́į́ góneʼ dóó sǫʼ siláágóó dóó ńléí tséhootsooíjįʼ.

en: That was probably their plan.
nv: koshį́į́ átʼéego bee hazʼą́ągo.

en: But the people who live over beyond yonder mountain in the area of Cove and Red Rock were thinking ugly thoughts about the plan in connection with education.
nv: ńtʼéeʼgo nagháí dził bineʼjí kʼaabizhii dóó tsé łichííʼ dah azkání nahósʼaʼgi diné kéédahatʼínígíí óltaʼ wolyéii baa chʼíhwiitʼaahgo shį́į́ yikʼee dadiniihgo ntsídaakees lá.

en: It is just recently that these people became old men, and they have all died.
nv: éí tʼáá ániidígo hastóí dajizlį́įʼgo ałtso ádajidin.

en: At that time, when the boys acted as they did, they were young men.
nv: íídą́ą́ʼ ashiiké dajílį́įgo ádajíítʼįįd.

en: The children said that if this business of taking children to school got to them they would really do something about it.
nv: áłchíní óltaʼgóó adahatʼéésh haʼnínígíí tʼáá nihitah ńtʼiʼí bíniʼ biniinaa háágóó ániitʼée dooleeł.

en: As we came to find out, they were saying that would not get a one of their children.
nv: nihaʼáłchíní doo łaʼ haa diiltéeł da dajiníigo shį́į́ átʼéé lá.

en: A man by the name of Black Horse was the leader of that faction.
nv: bilį́į́ʼ łizhinii joolyéé ńtʼééʼ éí áájí ákótʼéego bee dah ajooʼish ńtʼéé.

en: They had no doubt heard that in a certain number of days a party would come to Blue Clay Point for the purpose
nv: bis dootłʼizh deezʼáhí hoolyéegi ákwíí yiską́ągo biniiyé ínééh jiní díí áłchíní óltaʼjįʼ ndahaʼniłígíí kótʼéego shį́į́ dajííniiʼ.
of putting children in school.	from a navajo corpus of historical narratives 21.7

en: So they began to think of the matter with bitterness.
nv: áko shį́į́ hwiiʼ ndahodikʼǫǫshgo tsídazhdeezkééz.

en: “Boys, let’s go there. Come on!”, they probably said.
nv: “ashiiké, díkwídiiltʼeeł lá. ákǫ́ǫ́ dooleeł,” dazhdííniid shį́į́ lá áádę́ę́ʼ.

en: So they probably set out from there for this purpose.
nv: áko shį́į́ áádę́ę́ʼ biniiyé dashdiikai.

en: We had not heard of this and knew nothing about it.
nv: éí nihí doo deiiʼniih da dóó doo nihił béédahózin da lá.

en: They met at Blue Clay Point near the trading post there was a house which, at that time, we called the Ugly House.
nv: éí bis dootłʼizh deezʼáhígi adááh jíkai silį́į́ʼ lá naalyéhé bá hooghan dóó tʼáá áhánígi kin łaʼ siʼą́ íídą́ą́ʼ kin hóchxǫ́ʼí dahodiiʼní.

en: The house served the purpose of providing a place to sleep for the people who came to the trading post.
nv: diné naalyéhé bá hooghangi ńdaakahii yiiʼ ńdanjah biniiyé kin siʼą́.

en: Black Horse's party went over there, and they no doubt came with evil thoughts. The people who, lived hereabout had heard nothing of their plans, but at night they spoke about themselves, revealing their intentions.
nv: áájí shį́į́ jíkai lá. tłʼéeʼgo shį́į́ ákótʼéego bee ádaa ndahojisneʼastóí tʼáá kǫ́ǫ́ kéédahatʼíinii éí doo há deiniih da. tłʼéeʼgo shį́į́ ákótʼéego bee ádaa ndahojisneʼ.
